History:
- Presenting complaint: Widespread sore, red, very itchy, dry skin consistent with an eczema flare.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began over the past few days and have become markedly worse during that time.
- Distribution: Chest, hands, arms, worst in the inside of the elbows.
- Local findings reported: Cracked skin in some areas; no weeping/ooze; no visible scratch marks; no thickened/darkened skin.
- Associated/systemic symptoms: No fever or joint pain reported.
- Triggers/previous episodes: History of eczema with prior similar episodes.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic conditions: Eczema (history), asthma (intermittent use of reliever "blue" inhaler PRN).
- Family history: Mother with hypothyroidism and migraine.
- Allergies: Denies drug allergies.
- Current medications and skin-care: Diprobase emollient (uses daily), "Dermal" shower product (uses in shower), topical hydrocortisone OTC (used; dose/route/frequency not documented), intermittent use of blue inhaler PRN. Patient reports having tried an OTC antihistamine (possibly cetirizine) previously and found it ineffective.

Physical Examination:
- No formal clinician-recorded vitals or physical exam documented.
- Patient-reported/observed skin findings: widespread erythema, dryness, intense pruritus, focal skin cracks; no weeping, no scratch marks, no lichenification reported.
- General: Patient conversational and ambulatory in video consult; no fever reported.

Impression:
- Widespread eczema exacerbation (acute flare).

Management Plan:
- Prescriptions:
  - Fexofenadine (antihistamine) — prescribed; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Topical betnovate (potent topical steroid) — prescribed. Instructed application: small fingertip-unit amount to affected areas; apply twice daily for the next couple of weeks.
- Continue regular emollient therapy (Diprobase) and Dermal wash as ongoing skin care.
- Prescription sent to Boots pharmacy for collection.
- Advice: If no improvement after two weeks, or if symptoms worsen or an adverse/allergic reaction occurs, contact the service earlier. Return for review if needed.

Patient Summary:
- The patient with a known history of eczema developed a widespread, progressively worse flare over several days affecting chest, hands, arms (worst in elbow flexures). The plan is short-term escalation of topical steroid therapy (betnovate) plus an oral antihistamine (fexofenadine) while continuing emollients; reassess if no improvement in two weeks or sooner if deterioration.

Key Takeaways:
- Start prescribed fexofenadine (antihistamine) and topical betnovate as directed.
- Continue daily emollients (Diprobase) and use Dermal in shower.
- Return or contact sooner if symptoms worsen or if an adverse reaction occurs; otherwise review after two weeks.

Next Steps:
- Patient to collect prescriptions from Boots pharmacy.
- Re-evaluate in two weeks if no improvement; earlier contact if worsening or adverse effects.
- No further investigations or referrals documented in this consult.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs, clinician-performed skin examination details, specific doses/routes/frequencies for fexofenadine (not documented) and for topical hydrocortisone (previous usage), exact name/dose of prior OTC antihistamine, and medication reconciliation details.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Antihistamine use: initially patient indicated no antihistamines currently, later stated having tried an OTC antihistamine and it was not effective (conflict noted).
  - Steroid use: patient variably states having used steroids before and there is ambiguity whether he is currently regularly using a topical steroid (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Mostly intelligible but portions were inaudible or fragmented; patient name not verbally confirmed in the transcript; some medication names and details were uncertain.
